What

What Residential Tree Removal Involves

Residential tree removal is the complete elimination of a tree on a single-family property — including in-person hazard assessment, permit verification (Pepper Pike, Moreland Hills, Gates Mills), felling or top-down dismantling, full chip haul-off, and site cleanup. Every residential removal Aaron walks includes a free written estimate with confirmed pricing before you ever commit.

The distinction that matters: residential means the crew, the equipment, and the process are scaled to homes rather than commercial or municipal sites. Bandit chipper on your driveway, Husqvarna saws, occasional crane rental only when structural rigging demands it. Most residential jobs are one-day work with a final walk-through before the crew leaves the property.

Why

Four Reasons Homeowners Call Roubic

The top scenarios Aaron walks each month across NE Ohio residential properties.

EAB-Killed Ash on the Property

Emerald ash borer wiped out most NE Ohio ash 2008–2012. Dead ash goes structurally unsafe fast — one growing season.

Tree Leaning Toward the House

Root plates saturate in wet springs. Wind shifts the load. Leaning trees over structures need proactive removal.

Storm-Damaged, Split Crown

Trees that survived one Cleveland storm rarely survive the next with a compromised crown. Better to remove before it fails.

Yard Redesign / Sunlight / Roots

Tree in the wrong spot — blocking driveway sightlines, roots lifting patio pavers, or overshadowing a garden bed.

Common Residential Questions

Residential Tree Removal FAQ

Five things NE Ohio homeowners want to know before booking.

Do I need a permit to remove a tree in my yard?
Depends on the village. Pepper Pike requires permit for trees 24" DBH or larger; Gates Mills 18"; Moreland Hills has its own rules. Auburn Township, Solon, Chagrin Falls (residential), Beachwood, Orange, Bainbridge Township, Shaker Heights, Chesterland, Mayfield, and South Russell — no permit needed for private-property residential removals. Roubic handles all permit filing in-house if required.
How long does a typical residential removal take?
Most single-tree residential removals finish in one day, including debris haul-off and site cleanup. Larger jobs (multiple trees, restricted access, or crane-required work) may run into a second day — Aaron confirms the timeline during the free estimate.
Do you handle the stump too?
Optional add-on. Stump grinding is $275 minimum plus $8 per inch of stump diameter, ground to 6–12" below grade. Full-excavation stump removal available for re-planting or hardscape installation. We can also leave the stump if that's what you want.
What if my tree is near a power line?
Trees touching or leaning into primary utility lines require the utility company to de-energize or send their line-clearance crew for the wire portion first. Roubic coordinates with the utility and handles the removal after wire clearance. It's a coordination job — but standard procedure for us.
Do you clean up all the debris?
Yes — standard residential job includes full chip haul-off with our Bandit chipper. Nothing left in your driveway. If you want the wood (for firewood or projects), we cut to specified lengths and stack. No price difference either way.
